The officials initially ruled Washington out of bounds inside the Saints’ one-yard line, but Raiders coach Klint Kubiak challenged the spot and won. Touchdown. Washington remains an elite bench stash and touchdown-dependent FLEX in Week 4 against the Chiefs.

item.title: Matt Hibner caught 2-of-2 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Matt Hibner BAL Tight End

Hibner came up with a 21-yard reception in the third quarter, but his biggest play came on a two-yard touchdown pass from Lamar Jackson as the Ravens were driving to take the lead. Hibner found just enough of a soft spot in the zone coverage for Jackson to sneak the pass in for the go-ahead touchdown, and now has three receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown on the season. The rookie fourth-rounder isn’t on the fantasy radar at this time and can be left on waivers ahead of Week 4’s game against the Titans.

item.title: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
item.description:
Cade Otton TB Tight End

As usual, Otton led the Bucs in pass routes and was second on the team in targets behind Emeka Egbuka. Most of Otton’s production came on a 37-yard catch in the first half. Baker Mayfield narrowly missed the tight end for another long gain later in the contest. Otton’s route involvement should keep him in deep league lineups next week against the Packers, unless Mayfield (hand) is sidelined.

item.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison ARI Wide Receiver

Harrison finished the day with a modest 3/40 receiving line, though that represents a small share of the Cardinals’ offensive output on the day. His first target was a declined offensive pass interference on third down and his first reception came in the second quarter. Harrison did make a clutch catch on third-and-long in the fourth quarter but he ultimately saw just five targets on a day where Jacoby Brissett threw 52 passes. Michael Wilson looks like Brissett’s preferred wide receiver while the deep looks Harrison can excel at are not easily obtainable in this iteration of the Cardinals offense. Harrison is a low-end fantasy WR4 at best against the Giants next week.

item.title: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints’ 27-35, Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding one rush for 36 yards and two lost fumbles.
item.description:
Tyler Shough NO Quarterback

Shough funneled four touchdown passes to Saints TEs Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, bringing the game’s total to six and tying a league record. The Saints’ quarterback played well overall, though his interception was due to a poor throw. Both fumbles were caused by Raiders pass rushers, and Shough had a third fumble reversed by an illegal contact penalty on the Raiders. Regardless, he can be trusted to throw the ball voluminously while adding a little extra with his legs. He warrants low-end QB1 treatment against the Falcons next week.

item.title: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals
item.description:
Pat Freiermuth PIT Tight End

Aaron Rodgers narrowly missed Freiermuth on a 20-plus-yard throw in the third quarter that could have been a touchdown if they had connected. Freiermuth has been targeted 14 times through the first three weeks but has just one meaningful fantasy line (5-45-1) thus far. Fantasy managers can find better options that Muth in Week 4’s game against the Browns.

item.title: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

Andrews missed part of this game with a hand injury but returned to catch two passes for a total of 15 yards in the second half. Andrews has yet to find the end zone this season and hasn’t gone for more than 49 yards in a game. There’s not much for fantasy managers to rely on here heading into next week’s game against the Titans.

item.title: Kyle Williams caught his lone target for 34 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Kyle Williams NE Wide Receiver

Williams logged a pass route on 16 of the Patriots’ 29 drop backs on the day and had one of the longest plays of the game for a struggling New England passing attack. Williams will need more playing time if he’s going to be viable for fantasy purposes. For now Mack Hollins appears to be the top wideout in the Patriots offense.

item.title: Ashton Jeanty rushed 19 times for 56 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints, adding three receptions for 37 yards.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Jeanty touched the ball four times on the Raiders’ opening drive before visiting with Raiders trainers while the Saints carried out their second possession. The medical staff taped both of Jeanty’s ankles and had him ready to go before the Raiders got the ball back. He came up grimacing after his ensuing carry, but remained active throughout all four quarters and totaled 21 touches on the day. He earned an end zone target on a wheel route early on, but the ball was overthrown. Jeanty might show up on the injury report this week, but he should be ready for an RB1-worthy workload against the Chiefs by the end of the week.

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) returned to the game in the second quarter of Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson departed after being tangled up on a target in the first quarter. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays but returned after missing only one drive. The talented youngster is coming off a career game in Week 2 as he looks to build momentum in the second game without Puka Nacua. He would ultimately depart again following his lone reception and would not return the rest of the game. Ferguson caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards prior to departing for good.

item.title: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
item.description:
Wan'Dale Robinson TEN Wide Receiver

Robinson got in the end zone for the first time as a Titan on a quick out route late in the fourth quarter. He comfortably led the team in targets and catches, though Carnell Tate beat him by one yard. Robinson and Tate are the only game in town for receiving opportunities on this team, but Cam Ward’s struggles make it hard to trust either for fantasy purposes. Robinson is a FLEX consideration in deeper leagues for his Week 4 matchup with the Ravens.

item.title: Zay Flowers caught 5-of-6 targets for 84 yards in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys, adding one carry for 20 additional yards.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers ran only 14 routes, but you wouldn’t know it by his production line. For a player dealing with a hamstring injury, he looked explosive every time he was on the field and turned three of his six touches into 20-plus-yard gains. Flowers hauled in a 22-yard pass in the first quarter to help set up a rush touchdown for Derrick Henry three plays later, and with time expiring in the fourth quarter, his 27-yard reception proved to be just enough to move Tyler Loop into position for the game-winning field goal with one second left on the clock. He’s only played in two games, but Flowers has been Lamar’s go-to target when on the field. His 48 percent targets per route run is one of the more absurd numbers you’ll find for any receiver. While that will eventually go down, there’s no denying he’s a must start whenever he’s active. Flowers will be in the mix as a high-end WR2 next week against the Titans.

item.title: Demond Claiborne had three rushes for one yard in the Vkings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
item.description:
Demond Claiborne MIN Running Back

Claiborne was the only Vikings back besides Aaron Jones to see a touch out of the backfield. DeeJay Dallas, meanwhile, was banged up coming into Week 3 and did not record a touch against the Bucs. Claiborne could see a fantasy-viable workload if Jones gets nicked up and Jordan Mason remains sidelined. He’s worth an add in deeper formats.

item.title: Aaron Jones had 17 rushes for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs, adding five catches for 34 yards.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Only Jordan Addison saw more targets than Jones, who retained his lead back role for a second straight week with Jordan Mason injured. Demond Claiborne was the only other Minnesota running back to see a carry (he had three). Jones was a grinder against the Bucs, picking up key first downs and shedding tacklers on screen passes in the second half. The Vikings seem intent on feeding Jones the rock for now. That should keep him in all lineups next week against the Dolphins.

item.title: Carnell Tate caught 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

The first-round rookie posted new high-water marks in every receiving category, though he did so while seeing fewer targets than Wan’Dale Robinson. Tate got going with a few chunk plays late in the game, setting up a Robinson touchdown and another scoring opportunity that was squandered by Cam Ward. Tate might be making incremental progress with this box score, but he’s still at the fringes of the WR4 discussion for Week 4 against the Ravens.

item.title: Michael Wilson caught 11-of-17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson saw season-highs across the board as the Cardinals played catch-up against the 49ers for much of the day. He operated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver, seeing over three times the opportunities as Marvin Harrison Jr. Catching much of the outside passes and intermediate crossers for the day, Wilson scored on a five-yard Jacoby Brissett pass in the third quarter. It’s clear he is Brissett’s top target in the offense, especially when the team is playing from behind. Wilson ranks as a high-end fantasy WR3 heading into Week 4 against the Giants.

item.title: Derrick Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Fantasy managers won’t balk at the production Henry provided their lineups in Sunday’s win over the Cowboys, but the Big Dog was largely bottled up against a suddenly stingy defensive front. Henry’s longest run came on a 29-yard burst in the third quarter that helped set up a Chris Moore receiving touchdown, but that run also accounted for 32.6 percent of Henry’s yards on the ground. He averaged a very underwhelming 2.4 YPC on his other 25 carries on the day and was tackled for a three-yard loss on a fourth-and-goal from the Cowboys’ one-yard line. The good news is Henry remains the unquestioned bell cow in the Ravens’ backfield, and he has a Week 4 revenge game against the Titans on tap. He’ll be a must start RB1 in what should be a plus matchup.

item.title: Kyler Murray completed 15-of-29 attempts for 168 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs, adding two rushes for 17 yards.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

In his first action since sustaining a concussion in Week 1, Murray wasn’t asked to do much in this one. He was about 4 percent below his expected pass rate on the day with an average depth of target of 9.4 yards. Murray targeted Jordan Addison heavily after Justin Jefferson left the game with an ankle injury, connecting with Addison on a 41-yard score and narrowly missing the speedy downfield wideout for another touchdown. Murray took three sacks and avoided a handful of other sacks against a Tampa front seven missing key players. Murray likely won’t be a 12-team starting play in Week 4 against the Dolphins even if Jefferson suits up.

item.title: Trey McBride caught 9-of-11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

McBride had a big receiving day, though penalties prevented it from being more productive. His first reception was called back due to offensive pass interference while he drew defensive pass interference in the endzone on a 4th-and-1 play. He continues to be the Cardinals’ most effective target on immediate routes, slashing through the 49ers defense for 75 yards. Not much more nuance is needed here, McBride is a fantasy TE1 for Week 4 against the Giants.

item.title: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

Mayer scored with just under six minutes left in the first half. Coach Klint Kubiak sent TE Brock Bowers in motion, back and forth across the formation, behind the line of scrimmage, before QB Kirk Cousins executed the play-action fake. Mayer ran an out route from the slot and shook S Justin Reid on the cut before quickly hauling in the pass. Mayer’s other two catches both went for double-digit yardage gains. He will be a viable high-end TE2 moving forward, with defenses focused on stopping Bowers.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Running a route on 29 of the team’s 37 drop backs, Hockenson was uninvolved in the offense even after Justin Jefferson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first half. Hockenson, who has nine grabs over the Vikings’ first three games, profiles as a low-floor weekly option in a Minnesota offense that has not passed at its usual volume early in the season.

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was taken to the locker room for x-rays in the first quarter of Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson got tangled up on a target half way through the first quarter and limped to the sideline under his own power. He was then escorted to the locker room for x-rays. No additional update has been provided.

item.title: Tyler Allgeier rushed two times for a loss of a yard in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers, adding four receptions for 10 yards.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

Allgeier lost nearly all high-value touches to Jeremiyah Love in Week 3, falling far behind the rookie in total opportunities and sinking further in total snaps. He saw 31 snaps to Love’s 55, seeing just six touches to Love’s 26. Allgeier’s most usage came in passing-down situations, catching four passes while pass-blocking was his most prominent role. Allgeier holds little standalone value with Love taking over the backfield; he is a valuable fantasy handcuff for now.

item.title: Jake Ferguson caught 3-of-5 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in Week 3’s loss to the Ravens.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson continues to make the most of his limited targets. Despite seeing just nine targets in his last two games, the veteran tight end has turned three of those into scores. Ferguson hauled in a 19-yard touchdown catch from Dak Prescott in the third quarter against the Ravens, but was otherwise held to just four yards on his other four targets. The touchdowns are encouraging, but we will need to see more targets before we can elevate Ferguson into TE1 territory. He’ll be a boom-or-bust TE2 next week against the Texans.

item.title: Jeremiyah Love rushed 21 times for 90 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers, adding five receptions for 19 yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love tallied a career-high 26 touches in Week 3, gashing the 49ers’ banged-up offensive line for over 100 total yards. The rookie out-snapped Tyler Allgeier 55-to-31 while also out-touching him 26-to-6. Nearly all the high-value touches went to Love, who scored on a play-action pass at the one-yard line. The path to true workhorse usage is wide open for Love after a monstrous workload and productive fantasy day against the 49ers. He is a high-end RB2 for Week 4 against the Giants.

item.title: Kenny Gainwell had three rushes for -4 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings, adding two catches for 14 yards.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell was once again inefficient with his limited opportunities. He operated as the team’s lead back, however, when Bucky Irving exited with a lower body injury. If Irving misses any time, Gainwell would profile as a top-24 PPR option, even if he loses touches to Sean Tucker. Tampa’s offense could be without Baker Mayfield (thumb) for a while. That would dampen the prospects of everyone in the offense.

item.title: Jordan Watkins caught both of his targets for 60 yards in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jordan Watkins SF Wide Receiver

Watkins saw increased opportunity with Mike Evans (rib) exiting in the second quarter. He caught a pair of long targets from Purdy despite KhaDarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing beating the 24-year-old in snaps. Watkins could certainly be on the fantasy radar if Evans misses an extended period of time.

item.title: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Tre Tucker LV Wide Receiver

Tucker had a bigger impact in real life than he did in fantasy. On the plus side, he helped set up a field goal and a touchdown, first by finding the soft spot in the Saints’ zone coverage in the two-minute drill. Later, his 15-yard gain on a deep crossing route helped set up the Raiders. He also committed a holding penalty, which erased a short gain for RB Ashton Jeanty. Tucker is a WR4/FLEX against the Chiefs next week.

item.title: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
item.description:
Elic Ayomanor TEN Wide Receiver

It goes down as his second one-catch, three-target, 11-yard game of the season. He posted those exact numbers in Week 1, though with a touchdown for good measure. Ayomanor popped for 69 yards in Week 2 but failed to find the big play in this game, cratering his numbers. As the WR3 on one of the worst offenses in football, he is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

item.title: Deebo Samuel caught zero passes for 80 receiving yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals. Yes, you read that correctly.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel’s box score will looks strange to most, but that’s what happens when Kyle Shanahan tries out a hook-and-ladder play in the first quarter. Mike Evans caught a pass from Brock Purdy, lateraling the ball to Samuel, who sprinted 80 yards downfield for the score. Despite Evans (rib) leaving the game early, Samuel technically finishes with zero targets, though he did carry the ball twice for 14 rushing yards. With his final stat-line, he sets the record for most receiving yards without a reception in NFL history. Samuel will benefit if Evans misses time and would be in the high-end WR3 range for Week 4 against the Broncos.

item.title: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said QB Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb and will undergo an MRI.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield is right-handed, so this injury could be consequential. The Buccaneers’ quarterback slammed his thumb into a Vikings defender this afternoon and remained down for a while after the play. UDFA rookie QB Jalon Daniels is next up on the depth chart and would be the presumptive starter next week against the Packers if Mayfield cannot play.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Bucky Irving had 15 rushes for 46 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings, adding two catches for 12 yards.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

Irving was on the sideline for much of the fourth quarter with a potential injury, though it was unclear when or how to picked up the ailment. He accounted for 15 of 18 Bucs running back carries on the day, maintaining his role as the clear No. 1 back in the Tampa backfield. He saw four targets while Kenny Gain well caught two of his five targets. Much of Gainwell’s involvement came after the Bucs fell behind the Vikings. Irving would have a sweet matchup in Week 4 against a vulnerable Green Bay defensive line if he can suit up.

item.title: Malachi Fields caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Malachi Fields NYG Wide Receiver

Fields hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game this year. He finished third on the team in targets in Week 3. Fields is on the field plenty, he just isn’t earning that many opportunities. He is not a viable fantasy option for Week 4.

item.title: Ethan Pocic (knee) exited in the fourth quarter of Week 3’s game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Ethan Pocic BAL Center

Pocic, who took a helmet to the knee, was already in the game to replace Jovaughn Gwynn, who exited earlier with an ankle injury. Now down both centers, the Ravens have called on rookie Vega Ioane to snap the ball for what is quickly becoming a decimated offensive line.

item.title: Baker Mayfield exited the Bucs’ Week 3 game against the Vikings with an apparent hand injury.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield was down for a while after taking a big hit from two Vikings defenders late in the fourth quarter, and replays showed his thumb slamming against one of the Minnesota players in a way that might suggest a serious thumb injury on his throwing hand. An extended absence for Mayfield could prove disastrous for Tampa’s pass catchers, as undrafted free agent QB Jalon Daniels would be the team’s starter. Mayfield threw for 217 yards, one touchdown, and one interception before his exit. Daniels would be an interesting superflex add considering his rushing ability.

item.title: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Darnell Mooney NYG Wide Receiver

Mooney has exactly two catches in each of his first three games as a Giant. He has hit on a few chunk plays in New York but isn’t seeing enough targets to be a weekly fantasy option. He is not on the FLEX radar for Week 4.

item.title: Raiders ruled out Jack Bech in Week 3 against the Saints with a forearm injury.
item.description:
Jack Bech LV Wide Receiver

Bech reportedly fractured his forearm against the Saints. Bech earned an end zone target on the Raiders’ fourth drive. The pass was overthrown and ruled incomplete, but Bech was hit by a defender late, resulting in a personal foul. The Raiders accepted it, erasing Bech’s target from the box score along the way. He finished the game with zero statistics and will likely miss a few weeks due to injury.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) is inactive for Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua came into the weekend listed as doubtful but was seen working out before the game to see if he would be able to go. He’ll ultimately be held out for the second consecutive game as the Rams look to improve to 2-1. Davante Adams vaults into the top-tier WR1 range in Nacua’s absence. Also inactive for the Rams are DB Kam Kinchens, WR CJ Daniels, WR Tutu Atwell, QB Ty Simpson, S Maximus Pulley, and OL Bill Murray

item.title: Greg Dulcich caught 5-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Greg Dulcich MIA Tight End

Held under 20 yards in each of the Dolphins’ first two games, Dulcich finally had something of a pop-up effort as the ‘Fins tried in vain to match points with the Chiefs. It was nice to get some proof of TE2 concept, but it is going to be exceptionally difficult for Dulcich to carve out streamer value in a low-volume passing attack focused on seeing what it has in its intriguing rookie receivers.

item.title: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-5 targets for 13 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely’s yardage total came back to Earth last week with just 33 despite seeing 10 targets. It fell further today, as did the target total. On the plus side, he finished second on the team in receiving opportunities and finished with a 23 percent target share. Likely remains the team’s de facto No. 2 receiver behind Malik Nabers. That simply wasn’t worth much in terms of fantasy points today. He remains a solid TE1 bet for Week 4 against the Cardinals.

item.title: Broncos declared WR Marvin Mims, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Sai’vion Jones, and DT Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 3 against the Rams.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims will be inactive for the second consecutive week while Humphrey’s presence is not required with the four receivers ahead of his on the depth chart active. Defensive lineman Sai’Vion Jones will have to wait to at least Week 4 to return.

item.title: Malik Washington caught 5-of-10 targets for 56 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, adding two carries for five yards.
item.description:
Malik Washington MIA Wide Receiver

Every total was a new season high for Washington, including the carries. It briefly appeared Washington might be the Dolphins’ emergency lead back, as De’Von Achane was knocked out with a knee injury and Ollie Gordon was cramping. With Achane seemingly set for a long absence, Washington could indeed be in line for more rushing usage. That makes him a slightly more viable WR4, but rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas still offer more overall upside heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. That’s, of course, if Douglas returns from his ankle injury.

item.title: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Emmett Johnson KC Running Back

Johnson was not targeted in the passing game. His six carries were nothing to sneeze at on an afternoon where the Chiefs were limited to 49 total plays, but that was compared to 20 Kenneth Walker touches. Johnson will have some pop-up standalone value behind workhorse Walker, but he is primarily a contingency option heading into the meat of the fantasy campaign.

item.title: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-5 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf has yet to crack 40 yards in a game this season, but he did manage to find the end zone for a six-yard touchdown late in the third quarter. The big plays have not been there for Metcalf thus far, who has a long catch of 16 yards. Metcalf will be on the WR3/WR4 radar for next week’s game against the Browns.

item.title: AJ Dillon rushed four times for 16 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
item.description:
AJ Dillon CAR Running Back

With Jonathon Brooks joining Trevor Etienne on injured reserve, Dillon was indeed the Panthers’ No. 2 back behind Chuba Hubbard. Good for him, though Pro Football Focus charted him with zero first half snaps. Were Hubbard to ever go down with injury, Dillion would form some sort of committee with a practice squad elevation or free agent addition.

item.title: Trent Williams (stinger) is questionable to return Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Trent Williams SF Tackle

Williams left in the third quarter, taking the cart to the 49ers locker room. The veteran left tackle was officially diagnosed with a stinger and is questionable to return. Vederian Lowe is in at left tackle with Williams out.

item.title: Darren Waller caught 5-of-8 targets for 51 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

With Xavier Legette (knee) sidelined and Jalen Coker (quad) joining him, Panthers tight ends Waller, Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined for 11/128. It was Waller’s most prolific receiving day of the season even though he didn’t find the end zone. Waller is undoubtedly providing valuable real-life reps for the Cats, but with 10 total receptions through three contests, he is looking like too much of a role player to rise above TE2 streamer status heading into Week 4 against the Lions.

item.title: John Metchie caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
item.description:
John Metchie CAR Wide Receiver

With a questionable Xavier Legette sidelined with a knee injury and Jalen Coker departing early with a quad issue, Metchie was forced into three-receiver sets alongside Tetairoa McMillan and “Brycen Tremayne.” His touchdown was an eight-yarder late where he found the soft spot in the end zone. The Panthers are undoubtedly happy Metchie stepped up, but with Legette likely to return for Week 4, Metchie isn’t worth a waivers look even if Coker is forced to miss time.

item.title: Jameis Winston complted
item.description:
Jameis Winston NYG Quarterback

The Giants rotated between punts and field goals in almost perfect succession throughout this contest. They leaned on their ground game with 33 carries compared to 22 pass attempts, so there wasn’t all that much for Winston to do. He took care of the ball with zero turnovers but had just one completion of more than 13 yards, a scramble drill toss to Cam Skattebo for 30. He will have to throw more often and more aggressively versus the Cardinals next week, but the Giants clearly don’t want him playing his normal, gunslinger brand of football. He will barely crack the QB2 ranks for Week 4.

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
item.description:
Tetairoa McMillan CAR Wide Receiver

By far McMillan’s quietest outing of the young season came with Jalen Coker departing midway through with a quad injury. No. 3 Xavier Legette didn’t even suit up as he battled a knee issue. That allowed the Browns’ defense to key in on T-Mac, and key they did. Fill-in No. 2 Brycen Tremayne took advantage with four receptions for a team-leading 83 yards. Heinous stuff for McMillan managers, but he has an immediate Week 4 bounce-back spot in the defense-less Lions.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers dominated looks from Trevor Lawrence on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Strange played his usual role as a check down option for Lawrence, rumbling for yards after the catch on two of his three grabs. Strange, with seven catches on the year, could be a streaming play in Week 4 against the Bengals if the game turns into a shootout.

item.title: Najee Harri rushed nine times for 52 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Najee Harris NYG Running Back

Devin Singletary was inactive this week and Tyrone Tracy only touched the ball once, leaving nearly all of the backup running back touches to Harris. He gashed the Titans for 5.2 yards per carry but wasn’t involved in the receiving game, limiting his fantasy value. Harris is the clear backup to Cam Skattebo, but he won’t see enough touches to be worth a FLEX spot when the Giants take on the Cardinals next week.

item.title: Vikings ruled out Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Jefferson picked up the ankle injury in the second quarter. He limped to the locker room shortly before halftime and was officially ruled out midway through the third quarter. Hopefully for the Vikings it’s not a long-term issue for the centerpiece of their offense. Jordan Addison would be the de facto No. 1 wideout if Jefferson misses time with the ankle injury. He caught a long touchdown from Kyler Murray against Tampa shortly after Jefferson left the game.

Source: Ben Goessling

item.title: KC Concepcion caught 2-of-9 targets for nine yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion caught 2-of-9 targets for nine yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers.

Well that’s not going to cut it. As ESPN’s Mike Clay points out, rookie first-rounder Concepcion is up to 20 targets over three appearances but has just 80 yards to show for it. He is not being put in position to make explosive plays, and he is very much not doing so. With a yards per catch more befitting of a sluggish running back (6.6), Concepcion is best left outside the WR4 ranks ahead of a tough Week 4 date with the Steelers.
item.rw:position: Concepcion caught 2-of-9 targets for nine yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers.

item.title: Denzel Boston caught 2-of-4 targets for 41 yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Boston’s 41 yards were his fewest in three games as a pro, though he has now contributed at least one 20-yard catch all three times out. On the rare occasions Deshaun Watson actually throws down-field, he’s looking only for Boston. That will lead to some spiked weeks, but Boston’s floor is too low to rank him inside the top 36 on a regular basis, including Thursday’s short-week home date with the Steelers.

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-7 targets for 33 yards in the Commanders’ Week 3 win over the Seahawks.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs didn’t catch any passes in the first half on his three targets, but “bounced back” in the final two quarters to turn a disaster of a game into a middling one. The wideout was able to score two touchdowns in Week 2 against Dallas, but was closer to non-factor than threat against a tougher Seattle defense. He’ll look to rebound and find the end zone again as the second option behind Terry McLaurin against the Colts in London in Week 4.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Quinshon Judkins rushed 18 times for 70 yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers, adding two receptions for nine yards.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

Both Judkins’ carries and yards were new season highs, though so was his 3.9 yards per carry. That tells you all you need to know about his explosive-play odds in this low-ceiling attack. Judkins at least remains unchallenged for touches. Judkins’ usage gives him a low-end RB2 floor, but the same seems true of his ceiling. The Steelers are not a good Week 4 matchup for the Dawg Pound.

item.title: Cam Skattebo rushed 20 times for 60 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans, adding three catches for 40 yards.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

With the Titans struggling to amass more than a handful of first downs, John Harbaugh was more than happy to grind out three yards per carry with his lead back for the better part of four quarters. Skattebo’s only explosive play came on a downfield shot from Jameis Winston. Skattebo got open deep while Winston fled the pocket and the two connected for a 30-yard gain. That alone was enough to make Skattebo the team’s leading receiver. Skattebo’s strong workload will keep him in the RB2 ranks for Week 4 against the Cardinals, even though the offensive environment has taken a massive hit with Jaxson Dart out for the regular season.

item.title: Hunter Henry caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

With Eli Raridon sidelined, Henry still wasn’t part of the Patriots’ passing attack. Drake Maye threw one of his two picks on an end zone target to Henry. With seven catches through three games, Henry should remain on waiver wires ahead of the team’s Week 4 game against Buffalo.

item.title: Mike Evans caught 3-of-6 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 3 game against the Cardinals before exiting with a rib injury.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans exited in the second quarter of the 49ers’ Week 3 game against the Cardinals after taking a hard hit to the torso. The veteran entered the day questionable with a hip injury but played and had a productive day before leaving. Evans caught three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown at the time of his departure, pitching one of his catches to Deebo Samuel for a hook-and-ladder touchdown. The team ruled Evans out after halftime with a rib injury.

item.title: Xavier Worthy caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Xavier Worthy KC Wide Receiver

Worthy was also shaken up by a big hit but was never announced with an injury. Patrick Mahomes attempted only 24 passes this afternoon, but that’s still a disappointing target total for the third-year pro. 23-year-old Worthy is now sitting on just 10 catches for 63 yards through the Chiefs’ first three games. Even with this offense showing major year-over-year improvement, it’s getting harder to keep the WR4 faith with Worthy. The Raiders are a plus Week 4 matchup in Vegas.

item.title: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams was technically the team’s No. 2 receiver today because of the absence of Adonai Mitchell. The role amounted to almost no presence in the box score as Geno Smith simply peppered his tight ends with the targets left behind by Mitchell. Williams is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4 despite the uptick in snaps.

item.title: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-2 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Both Kelce’s catches and targets were his fewest of the young season, though he made them count on an afternoon where Patrick Mahomes dropped back only 25 times. Kelce notched a 48-yard catch-and-run on the first offensive play of the game, then finished off the Chiefs’ last real drive with an 11-yard touchdown grab in the back of the end zone. Why he went so long between looks can be a question for another day. Sitting on 231 yards receiving through the Chiefs’ first three contests, Kelce will remain a strong TE1 for Week 4 in Vegas.

item.title: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
DeMario Douglas NE Wide Receiver

Douglas was second on the team in targets behind only Mack Hollins, who saw nine looks from Drake Maye. Douglas got open and made a nice grab for his 38-yard gain — one of the only big plays for the struggling New England offense on Sunday. Though Douglas is playing a decent snap share, he should remain on waivers in most formats ahead of the Patriots’ Week 4 game against Buffalo.

item.title: Jeremy Ruckert caught all five of his targets for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Jeremy Ruckert NYJ Tight End

Kenyon Sadiq was the primary beneficiary of Mason Taylor’s absence with a 7/105/1 receiving line, but Ruckert was also part of Frank Reich’s plan to replace Taylor’s snaps. He posted career highs in catches and yards while scoring his second touchdown since entering the NFL in 2022. Ruckert isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 4, but he’ll be a solid role player for the Jets if Taylor remains sidelined.

item.title: Braelon Allen rushed four times for 14 yards in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions, adding three catches for three yards.
item.description:
Braelon Allen NYJ Running Back

Breece Hall suffered a thigh injury late in this game and did not return, leaving Allen as the lead back for the Jets’ final two drives. He touched the ball six times on the pair of drives. Fellow backup Isaiah Davis saw one touch in the entire game and it was before the Hall injury. His role would likely grow if Hall misses time, but Allen is the clear target in his backfield on waivers. Allen would push for an RB2 ranking if Hall is sidelined for Week 4 against the Bears.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez had eight rushes for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez remained the second option in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten, but stole a short score from Tuten in the blowout victory. Through three games Rodriguez has been a between the tackles option who has next to no involvement in the passing game. He would only be fantasy viable if Tuten misses time this season. For now C-Rod is a decent stash as a contingency option.

item.title: Ollie Gordon rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, adding three receptions for 14 yards.
item.description:
Ollie Gordon MIA Running Back

Gordon entered this afternoon with only three touches all season, but was pressed into every-down duty after De’Von Achane suffered a potentially serious knee injury on the game’s opening series. Fellow backup Jaylen Wright was inactive with a foot issue. Gordon mostly held up well, though he himself briefly went into the locker room with cramping issues. He returned after getting an IV. With Achane evidently staring at a long absence, Gordon is a priority waivers add, though he and Wright will undoubtedly form a committee for this undermanned offense. The question is who gets the strong side. It wouldn’t be surprising if Wright assumed primary early-down status with Gordon changing the pace. That would require Wright being healthy, of course. We will keep you updated.

item.title: Chris Bell caught 4-of-7 targets for 67 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

With Caleb Douglas sidelined with an ankle issue, talented third-rounder Bell finally broke out after totaling just one catch for 25 yards through the Dolphins’ first two contests. The No. 94 overall pick looked big and explosive with the ball in his hands, and could have had a much bigger day had Malik Willis been able to find him on what might have been a pair of long touchdowns. Bell’s box scores figure to remain inconsistent going forward — Willis is a dual-threat quarterback with a bevy of young, unproven wideouts — but he is certainly worth taking a flier on if currently un-rostered in your 12- team league. Bell’s pre-draft profile as a size/speed menace who only fell because of his torn ACL looked 100 percent accurate against the Chiefs.

item.title: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta was a secondary piece of the passing attack in this game, taking a backseat to Jhamyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The two superstars combined for 16 targets while LaPorta and Jameson Williams were held to a combined eight looks. LaPorta has at least 44 yards in every game this year but no more than 52. With a solid floor established, all that’s left is for LaPorta to hit on a ceiling game. He remains a mid-range TE1 for Week 4 against the Panthers.

item.title: Cowboys S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 3 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Jalen Thompson DAL Safety

Thompson left the field after getting caught up in a scrum that initially looked like a potential head/neck injury. It was later reported as a hamstring injury, with sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson saying the 28-year-old safety was struggling to make his way to the locker room. It sounds like Thompson could face an uphill battle to return to the field in this one. The Cowboys’ defense continues to be dealt one injury after another. Markquese Bell is next in line to replace Thompson.

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans was carted off in the second quarter of Week 3 against the Cardinals with an apparent torso injury.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans took a major hit in the second quarter against the Cardinals, with Budda Baker jarring the veteran receiver in his torso. Trainers came out and took Evans off the field; he was seemingly struggling to breathe as he headed to the sideline. It is unclear yet what the injury is, but Evans was carted to the locker room shortly after. He had caught 3-of-6 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown at the time of his departure, with one of his catches leading to a pitch to Deebo Samuel on a hook-and-ladder touchdown.

item.title: Jared Goff completed 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-24, Week 3 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Jared Goff DET Quarterback

Goff and the Lions got off to a slow start with just three points over their first three drives. Things started to click before halftime and Goff rode that momentum to 21 points after the break. Excluding a few kneel-downs to end the game, Detroit scored on five of their final six drives. The Lions have scored exactly 31 points in all three of their games this year. That may be a bit higher than their projection for Week 4 against the Panthers, but not by all that much. Goff will remain in the QB1 mix versus Carolina next week.

item.title: Mark Andrews (hand) is questionable to return in Week 3 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

We’re not quite sure what happened here, but Andrews was not on the field for the Ravens’ fifth drive of the game, with the team announcing soon after that he would be questionable to return. The veteran tight end caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards before exiting.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: Rashee Rice caught 7-of-9 targets for 88 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice’s seven receptions were easily a new season best, though he’s now cleared 80 yards in back-to-back contests. Rice’s nine targets were no joke on a day where Patrick Mahomes was limited to 24 attempts as the Chiefs ran just 49 plays. Rice was also the intended target on Mahomes’ “interception,” which in reality was a ball Rice batted into the air. Not good, but neither was the pass. It was behind the wideout, who was laying on the ground. We doubt Mahomes holds it against him. Rice will remain a solid WR2 for Week 4 in Vegas.

item.title: Parker Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
item.description:
Parker Washington

It’s Washington’s second touchdown in the Jags’ first three games of the season. Washington caught his touchdown against the Patriots after having an acrobatic touchdown grab called back on a penalty. Having established himself as the team’s clear-cut WR1 — well ahead of Brian Thomas, who had one target in Week 3 — Washington will have a rock solid weekly floor with ceiling to spare in shootout game scripts. Washington should remain in all lineups next week against a middling Bengals defense, in what could be a high-scoring affair between two potent offenses.

item.title: Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch any of his three targets in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Oronde Gadsden II LAC Tight End

Gadsden’s first target of the day was on a third-down pass that hit off his hands and landed on the grass. Neither of his other two targets was particularly close to being caught. He did play on 39 of the team’s 69 snaps, more than any other tight end, and ran a route on 31 of their 43 dropbacks, which was the third-most of any player on the Chargers. I guess you can talk yourself into his role based on those numbers, but the results weren’t there, and the Chargers look discombobulated on offense. It’s hard to trust Gadsden in fantasy going forward.

item.title: Kenneth Walker rushed 18 times for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for three yards and a second score.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

The two-touchdown outing was Walker’s second in three games as a Chief after he had only one such effort for the Seahawks last season. His 20 touches were a rather remarkable total seeing as the Chiefs were limited to 49 plays with the Dolphins attempting to play keep away. He was not efficient, but Patrick Mahomes was. That’s the new reality for defenses facing the Chiefs, as this is no longer a stop Mahomes at all costs team. You now have to pick your poison, which is going to lead to many more blow-up efforts for KWIII. Perhaps that will include Week 4 in Vegas against the Raiders.

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson had seven rushes for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding three catches for 16 yards.
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

TreVeyon Henderson, meanwhile, had eight rushes for a meager 23 yards in the blowout loss to Jacksonville. Stevenson ran most of the pass routes out of the backfield and saw more targets than Henderson, as usual. It didn’t lead to much. Stevenson next week against the Bills will be a touchdown dependent RB3 option who should be kept on the bench in most fantasy formats.

item.title: Isaac TeSlaa caught all three of his targets for 66 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Isaac TeSlaa DET Wide Receiver

TeSlaa led the Lions in receiving on the back of a 49-yard grab late in the game. He was otherwise an afterthought in the offense, finishing the game with a nine percent target share. TeSlaa is averaging three targets per game, which simply isn’t enough to get him into the FLEX mix. He is buried in the WR6/7 range headed into Week 4.

item.title: Tre’ Harris caught 6-of-7 targets for 76 yards receiving in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Tre' Harris LAC Wide Receiver

This is the second game in a row that Harris has led the Chargers in receiving, but this was not simply because of one catch, like last week. Harris looked good in this one, making a few nice hands catches and showing some ability to gain yards after the catch. He only ran a route on 27 of the team’s 43 dropbacks, but with the team now 0-3, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see the Chargers try to get Harris involved more next week against the Seahawks. Even if he doesn’t produce in a tough matchup, he’s worth a bench stash in most league types.

item.title: Quentin Johnston caught 3-of-6 targets for 40 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Quentin Johnston LAC Wide Receiver

Johnston also had a really bad drop on a 3rd-and-10 pass in the fourth quarter with the Chargers trailing. The ball hit him directly in the hands about three yards past the sticks, and he dropped it. Still, Johnston played on 60 of the team’s 69 snaps and ran a route on 37 of their 43 dropbacks, so he remains the clear second receiver by playing time. After Week 3, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Tre Harris start to cut into Johnston’s workload.

item.title: DeeJay Dallas (toe) is active for Week 3 against the Bucs.
item.description:
DeeJay Dallas MIN Running Back

Dallas was the only Minnesota running back besides Aaron Jones to see a backfield touch last week with Jordan Mason sidelined with injury. Dallas wouldn’t hold fantasy value unless Jones gets dinged up. Vikings declared T Caleb Tiernan, DT Elijah Williams, CB Zemaiah Vaughn, S Jakobe Thomas, S Tavierre Thomas, and P Brett Thorson inactive against the Bucs.

Source: Tanner Weber

item.title: Breece Hall suffered a thigh injury in Week 3 against the Lions and will not return.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Hall was thrown to the ground on a red zone carry early in the fourth quarter and immediately grabbed at his thigh. He was slow to get up and left for the medical tent. The team ruled Hall out rather quickly, possibly signaling that the injury is serious. Braelon Allen will see the bulk of the touches for the remainder of the game.

item.title: Bucs declared OLB Rueben Bain, LB Josiah Trotter, DL Rakeem Nunez-Roches, CB Ayden Garnes, G Luke Haggard, and G Billy Schrauth inactive for Week 3 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Rueben Bain TB Outside Linebacker

Both Bain and Trotter being out for the Bucs makes this matchup significantly easier for Kyler Murray and the Vikings offense. Tampa’s offense has struggled against the run too, meaning Aaron Jones should be in a good spot as the Vikings’ workhorse back with Jordan Mason sidelined.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Bills CB Christian Benford (toe) is questionable to return for Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

Benford was in coverage away from the ball when he planted to run forward and came up hobbling. He went down and then later gingerly walked off the field with trainers. Considering Benford previously missed games with a toe injury last season, this is something to monitor in the coming weeks. Davison Igbinosun will come in to take Benford’s place.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Dylan Parham suffered a knee injury in the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions and will not return.
item.description:
Dylan Parham NYJ Guard

Parham signed a two-year deal with the Jets in the offseason. Jordan Meredith has taken his spot at left guard. Needing a flurry of points to get back in this game, things are looking bleak for Gang Green.

item.title: Raiders declared S Treydan Stukes, QB Aidan O’Connell, CB Darrell Luter Jr., S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue and DT JJ Pegues inactive for Week 3 against the Saints.
item.description:
Treydan Stukes LV Safety

The Raiders will be without Stukes, their starting free safety, and Johnson, their backup strong safety, against the Saints. Keeping Saints WR Chris Olave and TE Juwan Johnson in check could be challenging.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Saints declared WR Barion Brown, QB Zach Wilson, CB Martin Emerson Jr., DL Christen Miller, TE Treyton Welch, DT John Ridgeway and EDGE Tyree Wilson inactive for Week 3 against the Saints.
item.description:
Barion Brown NO Wide Receiver

The Saints will be without their gadget player and return specialist, teeing up WR Bryce Lance for the full-time No. 3 wide receiver role. Brown is not relevant in 12-team leagues, though he may be missed by the Saints. Emerson, the Saints’ No. 3 cornerback, is sidelined by a shoulder injury.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Jalen Coker suffered a quad injury in Carolina’s Week 3 game against the Browns and will not return.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker was initially deemed “questionable” but then quickly ruled out. That’s never a good sign. Coker entered the proceedings battling an ankle issue, so this is a new injury. He departed midway through the third quarter. With Bryce Young playing through something, it’s been an extremely subdued day for the Panthers’ passing attack against a feisty Browns defense. Coker had just two catches for 18 yards on four targets before departing.

item.title: Leo Chanel was carted off in the first half against the Seahawks in Week 3 with a neck injury.
item.description:
Leo Chenal WAS Linebacker

Chanel was able to wave to the crowd as he exited, but obviously this is an injury that has potential long-term ramifications. He’ll likely be unavailable to go in Week 4 against the Colts in London.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) is active for Week 3 against the Saints.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers makes his debut in coach Klint Kubiak’s offense against the Saints today. The two-time Pro Bowl player should be started as a high-end TE1, although it might take a game or two for Bowers to get back into form. That said, it might not. He is an exceptionally talented player who should immediately function as his team’s top target earner.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) active for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans entered the weekend questionable for Week 3 after missing two practices and getting in one limited practice during the week. The veteran tends to rest minor injuries before playing in games, indicating his hip issue should not have a major impact on his output against the Cardinals. The 49ers declared QB Kurtis Rourke, DE Nick Bosa (calf), DL James Thompson (ankle), DE Romello Height (hand), LB Tatum Bethune, CB Ephesians Prysock, and OT Enrique Cruz Jr. inactive for Week 3 against the Cardinals.

item.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) will play in Week 3 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, Flowers is only expected to be on the field for “about 20-30 plays.” Given this piece of news, fantasy managers looking to play Flowers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a WR3/WR4 in what could be a low-volume day for the Ravens’ WR1. While Flowers is active, the Ravens have declared WR Elijah Sarratt, FS K’Von Wallace, LB Carl Jones, LT Ronnie Stanley, DT Aeneas Peebles, and QB Fagnano inactive for Week 3.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: De’Von Achane (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Dolphins’ Week 3 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
De'Von Achane MIA Running Back

Deemed questionable in the first quarter, Achane was officially ruled out to begin the second half. Obviously terrible news, though Achane did remain on the sideline in uniform, albeit sans his shoulder pads. Still, a player dealing with a long-term injury would typically remain in the locker room. Perhaps there is hope for Achane to suit up in Week 4 against the Vikings. But for now, fantasy managers need to consider second-year pro Ollie Gordon a must add. Jaylen Wright could also end up in the mix, but he’s inactive for Week 3 with a foot issue.

item.title: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, OL Josh Fryar, DL Andrew Billings, and WR Reggie Virgil inactive for Week 3 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Beck continues to be the Cardinals’ third quarterback and will be a gameday inactive for Week 3 behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Dadrion “Rabbit” Taylor-Demerson (back) is the main injury inactive against the 49ers.

item.title: Leo Chanel was carted off the field during Week 3’s game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Leo Chenal WAS Linebacker

Chanel was unable to continue after taking hit on a run play, and while he was being stabilized, he was able to wave to the crowd upon his exit. There should be an update on the severity of the injury before the end of Sunday’s game.

Source: Chris Russell

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Panthers CB Mike Jackson suffered a groin injury in Carolina’s Week 3 game against the Browns and will not return.
item.description:
Mike Jackson CAR Cornerback

Jackson was injured on a first quarter play where he was called for pass interference. He’s an every-snap player for the Panthers’ defense, so this will require dipping into the team’s depth.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: Colts EDGE Laiatu Latu (chest) left Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans and is questionable to return.
item.description:
Laiatu Latu IND Defensive End

Latu tried to return briefly after suffering the injury, but went into the locker room. It seems unlikely he’ll return. A pectoral injury is probably the main concern at this point.

item.title: De’Von Achane was forced from the Dolphins’ Week 3 game against the Chiefs with a knee injury and is questionable to return.
item.description:
De'Von Achane MIA Running Back

Achane planted awkwardly after a first series catch-and-run. He remained down on the field for an eternity before walking extremely slowly to the sideline. He then headed to the blue tent before slowly making his way to the locker room. Achane seemed to be trying to “walk it off,” but he also seemed to not be succeeding. He did not have the looks of a player likely to return, but he wasn’t really limping and did not require the assistance of a cart. Ollie Gordon is the only other Dolphins back dressed for Week 3. Stay tuned.

item.title: Colts K Spencer Shrader (groin) left Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans and is questionable to return.
item.description:
Spencer Shrader IND Kicker

Shrader (groin) left Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans and is questionable to return.

item.title: FOX’s Jay Glazer reports Tyson Bagent cleared concussion protocol but Case Keenum will start Monday against the Eagles.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

He said this on FOX’s pre-game show. Per Glazer, they couldn’t make Bagent the starter because he wasn’t involved in enough of the game planning, but with Caleb Williams now due to miss 3-4 weeks, Bagent could easily start Week 4’s game against the Jets. It’s also possible Bagent makes a relief appearance in Week 3 if Keenum looks rough. Bagent likely should be added in any superflex leagues where his concussion left him on the waiver wire.

item.title: Keon Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman was iffy headed into the weekend with an ankle injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Last week Coleman caught all six of his targets for 63 yards with DJ Moore sidelined with a shoulder issue. Moore is active for Week 3, meaning Coleman should remain on fantasy benches for now.

Source: Katherine Fitzgerald

item.title: Chargers declared S Elijah Molden, QB DJ Uiagalelei, OL Alex Harkey, G Kayode Awosika, TE Charlie Kolar, WR Brenen Thompson, and DT Dalvin Tomlinson inactive for Week 3 against the Bills.
item.description:
Elijah Molden LAC Defensive Back

This is not an ideal injury report for the Chargers. Molden is the team’s starting free safety, but he’s currently out with a hamstring injury, while Dalvin Tomlinson, their starting defensive tackle, is also out with a hamstring injury. That’s good news for Josh Allen, James Cook, and the Bills offense. On the offensive side of the ball, Charlie Kolar, their starting tight end, has a forearm injury, and starting left guard Kayode Awosika has a fibula injury. Pair that with starting linemen Trey Pipkins III and Tyler Biadasz already being on the injured list, and their Chargers offensive line is going to be short-handed against a Bills defense that welcomed back Ed Oliver on Sunday. That could ding Omarion Hampton’s production a bit.

Source: Alex Insdorf

item.title: Chiefs declared CB Chamarri Conner (knee), T Josh Simmons (back), TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DE Jack Pyburn and DE Tyreke Smith inactive for Kansas City’s Week 3 game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Chamarri Conner KC Defensive Back

Conner and Simmons, who both have now missed multiple weeks, were ruled out on Friday. The other five players are healthy scratches.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. (back) will not play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Who could have seen this coming? Porter has yet to suit up for a game this season, and it’s due to either a back issue, his current contract situation, or a mixture of the two. Teams have inquired about his availability via trade, but no deal appears on the horizon for the 26-year-old corner. In addition to Porter, the Steelers also declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Drew Allar, QB Willi Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, DE Kevin Jobity Jr., and DE Gabe Rubio inactive for Week 3.

item.title: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, TE Thomas Fidone II, OL J.C. Davis, DL Josh Tupou, DL Bobby Jamison-Travis, CB Deonte Banks, and S Tyler Nubin inactive for Week 3 against the Titans.
item.description:
Devin Singletary NYG Running Back

Singletary is a healthy scratch this week. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy are the backup running backs for New York. Singletary had nine carries and four catches in the first two weeks of the year. His absence could be a slight boost to Cam Skattebo, though Singletary’s touches may just be distributed to the other backups.

item.title: Colts declared CB Charvarius Ward (groin) active for Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans.
item.description:
Charvarius Ward IND Cornerback

Ward was the only questionable Colts player, but got in a full practice on Friday. Ashton Dulin (ankle) was ruled out on Friday. The other Colts inactives, all healthy scratches, are RB DJ Giddens, DE George Gumbs Jr., QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton and G Dalton Tucker.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) is active for Week 3 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

It was reported earlier on Sunday that Pittman was expected to suit up, so this isn’t much of a surprise. Despite being ready to go, Pittman will be hard to trust this week against a much-improved Bengals defense. He caught just three passes for 58 yards on three targets in his lone game this season and his best left on fantasy benches in most cases.

Source: Pittsburgh Steelers

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is active for Week 3 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers was able to practice late in the week and will suit up as the team’s WR3 against a tough New England coverage unit. It’s a revenge game for Meyers, who through Week 2 has a 6 percent target share and a 12 percent air yards share while running a route on 76 percent of the Jaguars’ drop backs. Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, S Jalen Huskey, LB Jack Kiser, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive against the Patriots.

Source: Demetrius Harvey

item.title: Texans declared G Ed Ingram (groin), WR Nico Collins (hamstring), EDGE Jadeveon Clowney (knee), T Nate Thomas, CB Collin Wright and TE Brevin Jordan inactive for Houston’s Week 3 game against the Colts.
item.description:
Ed Ingram HOU Guard

No surprises here; Trent Brown (knee/wrist) will play off a questionable tag. The other three injured Texans were ruled out on Friday. Ingram has not practiced since suffering a groin injury in practice last Wednesday and has to be considered questionable for Week 4 as well as this point; he’s the best run blocker on Houston’s line.

item.title: Ed Oliver (hip) is active for Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

Oliver was a late scratch from last Thursday’s game against the Lions when he hurt himself during pre-game warm-ups. It seems that he’s feeling good now and will have a great matchup against a Chargers offensive line that is missing multiple starters in the interior.

Source: Jenna Cottrell

item.title: Jets declared Adonai Mitchell (finger) inactive for Week 3 against the Lions.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

The Jets took things down to the wire with Mitchell but will ultimately hold him out for at least a week as he works through the finger injury. The Jets are now extremely thin at receiver with first-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr. on IR on top of the Mitchell injury. Isaiah Williams will take over as the team’s No. 2 receiver this week. Also inactive for the Jets are CB Nahshon Wright, TE Mason Taylor, LB Kiko Mauigoa, RB Kene Nwangwu, K Blake Grupe, and S Minkah Fitzpatrick.

item.title: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is active for Week 3 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

With Rico Dowdle (toe) out and Eli Heidenreich being a healthy scratch, Warren will split backfield touches with Travis Homer. Warren should be in for a big workload, making him a safe RB2 with upside against the Bengals.

Source: Pittsburgh Steelers

item.title: Dolphins declared RB Jaylen Wright (foot/stinger), WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), EDGE Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring), QB Brady Cook, DB Marcellas Dial Jr., G DJ Campbell and T Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Miami’s Week 3 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

CB JuJu Brents and WR Ryan Miller will play off questionable tags. Wright has fallen behind Ollie Gordon in the pecking order, though nobody is really making any fantasy hay in the Miami backfield given the talent surrounding them.

item.title: Xavier Legette (knee) is inactive for Week 3 vs. the Browns.
item.description:
Xavier Legette CAR Wide Receiver

Jalen Coker (ankle), meanwhile, is active. Legette made a big catch in Week 2, but he’s one of the only boats not rising with the tide of the Panthers’ ascending offense. He is off the radar in 12-team league fantasy, especially now that he’s injured.

item.title: Commanders declared QB Jayden Daniels, LB Frankie Luvu, LB Javontae Jean-Baptiste, G Sam Cosmi and TE Chig Okonkwo inactive for Week 3 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo is considered week-to-week with his hamstring injury. With Daniels out, Athan Kaliakamanis will be the backup signal-caller for Marcus Mariota against the Seattle defense.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) is active for Week 3 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

The belief all along was that Coker would play despite carrying a questionable tag into the weekend. Coker is a solid top-24 play this weekend after a hot start that has included 16 receptions for 204 yards and two touchdowns. While Coker is active, the Panthers did declare WR Xavier Legette, LB Devin Lloyd, S Nick Scott, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, OT Albert Reese, and DT Cam Jackson inactive for Week 3.

Source: Panthers.com

item.title: Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 3 against the Chargers
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Both DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) were listed as questionable on the final injury report, but both of them will suit up to play. There’s a chance that they could have their snap share managed as they play through injuries, but we’d have to assume they’re both relatively healthy if the Bills are going to put both of them on the field in an early-season matchup. You may just see a little more Khalil Shakir and Josh Palmer usage than normal. Moore remains the receiver with the most fantasy upside and could be a low-end WR2 with Shakir also being a solid WR3 in PPR formats given his role as a lower aDOT target-earner.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Patriots declared TE Eli Raridon, QB Behren Morton, OT Dametrious Crownover, DT Leonard Taylor III, EDGE Dre’Mont Jones, and S Craig Woodson inactive for Week 3 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

Raridon’s absence should provide a small bump for Hunter Henry, who has run a route on 63 percent of the Patriots’ drop backs and seen a target on 16 percent of those routes through Week 2. Raridon had been running around 20 percent of the team’s routes. Henry profiles as a deep league option for Week 3 against Jacksonville’s pass-funnel defense.

Source: Ethan Hurwitz

item.title: Seahawks declared S Julian Love, S Ty Okada, DL Brandon Pili, QB Jalen Milroe, WR Montorie Foster Jr. CB Avery Smith and LB Connor O’Toole in active for Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Julian Love SEA Safety

The Seahawks will be without both of their starting safeties for Week 3 against the Commanders. Rodney Thomas Jr. and AJ Finley will get the starts in their absence. Milroe will be the emergency third quarterback with Sam Darnold (glute) back in action.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tyjae Spears (ankle) will play in Week 3 against the Giants.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears got in a single limited practice this week but is good to go after making it through pre-game warmups unscathed. He will continue to back up Tony Pollard while pitching in on passing downs. Spears is a low-end RB4 for Week 3. Inactive for the Titans are OL Antonio Mafi, DL Jackie Marshall, OL Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, DB Jaylon Jones, and RB Michael Carter.

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Adonai Mitchell (finger) is expected to miss Week 3 against the Lions.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

We’ll get official word from the team in a few minutes. If Mitchell is indeed out, Isaiah Williams would step in as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq would also take on a larger role.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports DJ Moore (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore suffered an AC joint sprain in Week 2 and did not return to that game. He got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. He will suit up versus the Chargers, though it’s unclear how much the shoulder issue will affect him. Moore would normally be a solid WR2 option in this spot, but fantasy managers will likely want to treat him as a WR3 until we see how the shoulder injury impacts his play and usage.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he does not expect “an imminent return for Josh Jacobs.”
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacob’s current time on the Commissioner’s Exempt List is expected to count as time served toward an eventual suspension. Rapoport added, “If they get to the point where it’s five games, six games, maybe eight games, that might be when you’re looking at a potential return for Josh Jacobs.” The NFL is currently trying to obtain video footage of the incident from the Hobart/Lawrence police department. The victim in Jacobs’ case requested that it be sealed by a judge for privacy reasons, but that request was denied. Now the NFL has filed a FOIA request to obtain it. It seems like they won’t make any decisions on Jacobs’ suspension until they have viewed the video, which could take several more weeks to resolve.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Keon Coleman (ankle) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman returned to practice on Friday and was listed as questionable for today’s game. DJ Moore (shoulder) also looks likely to play through his questionable tag. Coleman stepped up last week with six catches for 63 yards on six targets. While he’s not on the fantasy radar as long as Moore suits up, Coleman could be a valuable role player for the Bills this year.

Source: Cameron Wolfe

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports “the hope is” that Tyjae Spears (ankle) will play in Week 3 against the Giants.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears got in one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable. Per Garafolo, the Titans want to see how Spears looks in warmups before making a decision. The Titans are playing at New York, where rain and winds are expected to be an issue. The field conditions could play a role in whether Spears suits up or not. If he doesn’t, rookie Nick Singleton would see a few extra touches.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jayden Daniels (elbow) is expected to return “at three weeks or sooner.”
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Daniels dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow in Week 2. He suffered the same injury last year and it functionally ended his season. The good news for Commanders fans and fantasy managers is that he is not undergoing surgery and wasn’t placed on injured reserve. Still, Daniels will miss a few weeks and then runs the risk of re-injuring the elbow after returning. Marcus Mariota will start until Daniels is healthy. Mariota is one of the league’s best backups, so the fantasy outlook for Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin shouldn’t be too much worse while Daniels is out.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports J.J. McCarthy and Justin Fields are on the list of quarterback options for the Giants.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

If you have ever thrown a football, get an agent and have them contact the New York Giants. McCarthy and Fields join a list that, per previous reports, already included Gardner Minshew, Mac Jones, and Jimmy Garoppolo. Schefter also named Brandon Allen, who was on the Giants’ roster during training camp, as an option. Jameis Winston will get the start in Week 3, but the journeyman passer looked downright awful in relief of Jaxson Dart last week. The team will be forced to make a move at quarterback if he struggles versus the Titans today. McCarthy would be a true Hail Mary for the G-Men, but he does have a strong tie to the Harbaugh brothers via his time at Michigan.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Brock Bowers (knee) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Saints, barring a surprise.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers will still need to test out his knee during pre-game warmups, but all signs point to him making his 2026 debut later today. The team heavily limited his workload during practice this week and could do so in his first game back from the late offseason meniscus trim. Still, if Bowers is active, fantasy managers have to get him in their lineups.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jalen Coker (ankle) “should play” in Week 3 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Xavier Legette (knee) remains a game-time decision. Both players were officially listed as questionable on Friday. Coker has gotten off to a red-hot start this year with 16 grabs for 204 yards and a pair of scores through two weeks. Even if he’s limited by the ankle issue, the production is too good to keep on the bench. He is, at worst, a WR3 for his date with the Browns.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Myles Garrett “was given a timeline of roughly six weeks for his recovery from knee surgery.”
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett attempted to play through the knee issue in Week 1 but was clearly bothered by the balky knee. He underwent a knee scope shortly after the Rams’ opener and was placed on injured reserve. It was initially expected to be closer to a four-week absence for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Now he’ll miss a bit longer than that, and Rapoport added that the team will be cautious with his return, so he could be sidelined beyond even the six-week timeline.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Evans (hip) plans to play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans has been trending in the right direction throughout the week, with Kyle Shanahan already telling reporters a few days ago that he has a good chance to suit up. The team officially listed him as questionable on their final injury report, but fantasy managers can assume he is playing for now. Evans could see his role scaled back slightly, but the 49ers are extremely thin at receiver, having lost Demarcus Robinson to an ankle injury most recently. Even at less than full strength, Evans remains in play as a fantasy WR2.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Lions and Cowboys “have begun making inquiries about the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.”
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Schefter noted that a handful of teams have called Pittsburgh, so it’s likely more than just Dallas and Detroit.
