item.title: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that Eagles WR DeVonta Smith “is warming up, but he isn’t in pads” on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

It sounds like Smith may end up being listed as a limited participant. We will learn more when the injury report comes out later today. Hopefully, this is just veteran rest as the Eagles gear up for a Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Bears. Eagles WR Dontayvion Wicks took a hard fall in Week 2 and missed a few plays. He later told reporters that he “will be good.” If Wicks is indeed good and Smith is not, Wicks would operate as the receiving corps’ top option.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is not practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

It puts him in a tenuous spot to play in Week 3’s game against the Giants. Spears will likely need some sort of practice participation on Friday to have a real shot at suiting up after missing each of the first two sessions of the week with this ankle injury.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Titans RB Tony Pollard (ankle) is practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Pollard could be in line for a boost if he plays and Tyjae Spears sits, as the Titans haven’t really shown much interest in using their other running backs so far. Nicholas Singleton played just six snaps last week. Pollard missed practice Wednesday but seems to be in line to play after today’s session.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Tank Bigsby (undisclosed) is not practicing on Thursday
item.description:
Tank Bigsby PHI Running Back

Journalists have videos of him working out on the side, so this doesn’t necessarily close the door on Bigsby playing on Monday Night, but it’s yet another Waiver Wire Week 3 rug pull possibility. With Saquon Barkley actually practicing, it’s possible Bigsby has zero standalone value this week against the Bears.

Source: Brooks Kubena

item.title: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) expects to play in Week 3 against the Bears.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Per McLane, Barkley is suited up and present at Thursday’s practice. This puts him on track to face the Bears on Monday Night Football. Barkley underwent an MRI earlier this week. Apparently, the results were good. The Eagles’ No. 1 running back should be good to go, although he may end up logging a limited session to begin the week, as a precaution.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) said his shoulder feels good and x-rays came back with positive results.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers speaking to the media is likely also good news for his availability on Sunday. The 23-year-old wideout is practicing and upgraded to full today, so he’s likely to be good to go and has a chance at avoiding a questionable tag on Friday altogether.

Source: SNY Giants

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) was seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

This is great to see. Bowers has now participated in three consecutive practices, dating back to last week. We do not yet know his participation level. He has been limited in his last two appearances. Bowers is seemingly on track to play in Week 3 against the Saints. Treat him as an elite TE1 if he takes the field on Sunday.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. said he did not request a trade and said he would play when healthy.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

It sounds like he’s still dealing with back flareups from time-to-time. Overall, it’s an encouraging sign for his availability in Week 3 that he spoke to the media, but Porter admitted that he did not know if he’d be ready to go against the Bengals. He remains questionable heading into Friday’s practice report even after doing everything today.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: Bills DT Ed Oliver (hip) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

Oliver now has a chance to face the Chargers in Week 3, though nothing is certain. The Bills’ star interior defender injured his hip during pre-game warmups last week and was unable to play. The Chargers’ banged-up offensive line has underperformed thus far. This is a situation worth monitoring.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

Raridon worked off to the side yesterday and ended up being listed as a limited participant. He is not seen with the team again today, so either a light, limited session or a total absence is possible. Either way, Raridon remains firmly in the questionable column, though a second limited session would theoretically put him on track to play in Week 3 against the Jaguars.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) was not spotted at practice on Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Neither was Keon Coleman. Moore grabbed a limited listing on Wednesday while wearing a non-contact jersey in practice; a downgrade would be troubling for his chances of playing in Week 3. Coleman (ankle) has now missed the first two days of the week and would need a comeback on Friday to get on the questionable line.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker is not wearing a uniform today, so we expect him to be a non-participant on the official injury report, which should come out in less than 90 minutes. We will provide an update if he ends up being listed as limited, or somehow inexplicably full. Coker played through the ankle injury last week, posting an 8/66 receiving line, so we like his odds of suiting up and playing effectively this week. This could just be a rest day. He was limited yesterday. Stay tuned.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas left the Giants’ Week 2 game against the Rams with a groin injury. He dealt with an ankle injury in practice last week. It is possible that fill-in starter, QB Jameis Winston, will be without his top pass protector in Week 3 against the Titans. Thomas was limited yesterday. It appears as though he will be a DNP today.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Dolphins WR Chris Bell (knee) was seen working off to the side on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

According to the Sun Sentinel’s David Furones, Bell mostly worked on the side and went inside before the portion of practice open to the media ended. Bell could end up being listed as a limited participant today, but he is clearly barely participating. It would not be surprising to see a DNP next to his name later today. He was limited yesterday. Bell underwent ACL reconstruction late last year. Hopefully, they are only managing soreness.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

We expect Douglas to be listed as a non-participant today, just like yesterday. Douglas got his ankle rolled up on in Week 2, which is always a concerning injury. Fortunately, his foot was only planted for a moment, so he may have avoided the worst-case scenario. He was later seen wearing a boot. The prudent move is to expect Douglas to miss Week 3. Fellow Dolphins WR Chris Bell (knee) will either be listed as a non-participant or limited, but it sounds like it would be a very light limited, if so.

Source: David Furones

item.title: When asked about Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen, WR coach Chad O’Shea said rookie wide receivers are “always a work in progress.”
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

You don’t say, Chad. Allen was the talk of Chiefs training camp. Beat reporters celebrated his ability to beat man coverage and win over the middle of the field — two aspects that help wide receivers thrive in fantasy. Unfortunately, Allen has logged just four offensive snaps this season. O’Shea adds that Allen is improving every day, both “fundamentally and schematically.” Good for him. The once-intriguing rookie is droppable in 12-team formats, though an in-season breakout remains possible. Theoretically.

Source: Charles Goldman

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Beat reporters observed Flowers working out on his own before practice, but the Ravens’ No. 1 wide receiver headed back inside the building before his teammates took the field. ESPN’s Jamison Hensley wrote, “it’s looking like Baltimore will be without Flowers for a second consecutive game.” The team downplayed Flowers’ Week 1 hamstring aggravation, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable. The Ravens depart for Brazil this evening and arrive on Friday morning. If Flowers travels, he may have a chance to play, though he will carry re-injury risk.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports, “Judge Marc Hammer denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.”
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

He added that the matter has been turned over to the Hobart/Lawrence police department, which is now in charge of determining whether or not the video will be released. Jacobs or the victim can then appeal that decision. The NFL has been adamant about getting the video before determining Jacobs’ pending suspension, and this increased the odds of that happening. Still, Jacobs could try to prevent that through the appeal process. Jacobs is believed to be facing a 4-6 game suspension, but the NFL can increase the length because of aggravating circumstances. This legal matter is inching toward a resolution, but a clash over the video would likely delay things even further.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Rico Dowdle (toe) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Penn Live’s Nick Farabaugh did note that Dowdle has shed his boot. He injured his toe in Week 2’s loss to the Pats but pushed through the issue in the second half. He was spotted in a boot on Wednesday. It looks like Dowdle will miss Week 3, but shedding the boot this quickly is a good sign that he isn’t dealing with a long-term issue. Jaylen Warren would vault into the RB2 ranks if Dowdle is ruled out before kickoff.

Source: Nick Farabaugh

item.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

After missing the first two sessions of the week, we fully expect Collins to be ruled out on tomorrow’s run of the injury report. No receiver caught more than three passes with Collins sidelined for Week 2. Dalton Schultz, on the other hand, exploded for 140 yards on 12 grabs and an absurd 14 targets. He is firmly in the TE1 ranks for Week 3 versus the Colts.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
item.description:
Gardner Minshew ARI Quarterback

Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run. Schefter noted that Minshew played under Giants OC Matt Nagy in Kansas City, giving him some familiarity with the team’s scheme. He also mentioned that it will not be cheap to pry Jones away from the 49ers. Jimmy Garoppolo is out there as well. He is a free agent and is reportedly still interested in playing, “in the right situation.” For now, the Giants are going to roll with Jameis Winston. Jake Haener will back him up. They will likely add someone as an extra backup option, but Winston is an interesting QB2 for fantasy purposes until they make a bigger addition.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “not making great progress.”
item.description:
Puka Nacua

In a surprisingly candid interview with ESPN Los Angeles, McVay certainly did not sound optimistic that Nacua would play in Week 3. Nacua has already missed one practice this week and there’s been no indication that he will get back on the field over the next two days. Davante Adams racked up 195 yards and two scores with Nacua out in Week 2. It will be hard not to rank him as a WR1 once Nacua is ruled out. Terrance Ferguson operated as the team’s No. 2 receiver last week and will be in the TE1 mix without Nacua.

Source: ESPN Los Angeles

item.title: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett (hip) was a full practice participant on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett ARI Quarterback

Brissett seemingly dealt with an injury in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss against the Seahawks, but played through it. He opens the week listed with a hip injury but was a full practice participant. Though Brissett seems to have a hip issue ailing him, it does not seem like it will keep him from playing. The veteran remains in the low-end QB2 conversation for Week 3 against the 49ers.

item.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) said his shoulder feels good and x-rays came back with positive results.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers speaking to the media is likely also good news for his availability on Sunday. The 23-year-old wideout is practicing, so he’s likely to be good to go and has a chance at avoiding a questionable tag on Friday altogether.

Source: SNY Giants

item.title: 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

Robinson suffered an ankle injury in the 49ers’ Week 2 win over the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was that the veteran would miss some time and his DNP designation Wednesday indicates just that. With Mike Evans (hip) also not practicing, the 49ers’ receiving corps is getting thinner than it already was.

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Kupp also opened last week with a limited practice due to the back injury before getting in two full practices and playing in Week 2. His limited designation Wednesday is likely a continuation of veteran workload management for his back; fantasy managers should not be surprised to see the 33-year-old limited on Wednesdays this season.

item.title: Commanders RB Kaytron Allen (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kaytron Allen WAS Running Back

Allen popped up on the injury report as a limited participant due to a hip injury. The rookie has seen limited touches as the Commanders’ third-string back and is still buried in the depth chart. Also limited was WR Jaylin Lane (groin). Lane is likely to play as he played through the injury in Week 2. Allen’s status is up in the air; practice reports from later in the week will paint a clearer picture.

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price entered Wednesday expected to practice and officially received a limited designation due to a chest injury he suffered in Week 2. Also limited was George Holani (knee). With both backs starting out limited, their Week 3 statuses are up in the air. If one or both can’t go, Emanuel Wilson is the primary beneficiary for fantasy purposes against the Commanders.

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold was officially listed as a limited practice participant on Wednesday, returning to practice for the first time since his opening day injury. He split first-team reps with Drew Lock and did some throwing off to the side. The Seahawks will make a decision Friday on Darnold’s game status for Week 3 but the 29-year-old has an outside chance of returning against the Commanders.

item.title: Bills DT Ed Oliver (hip) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

Oliver suffered a hip injury during warmups of the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions. He did not play in the game and now starts out Week 3 not practice. Oliver could certainly still go this week against the Chargers but he will likely need at least a limited practice to be in consideration to play.

item.title: Bills WR Keon Coleman (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman pops up on the injury report with an ankle injury and did not practice on Wednesday. He briefly left the Bills’ Week 2 game against the Lions due to the ankle, but returned and finished the game. Coleman’s status for Week 3 is now in jeopardy; with DJ Moore (shoulder) also on the injury report, the Bills’ wide receiver groups may look slim come Sunday against the Chargers.

item.title: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore was officially listed as limited after wearing a red non-contact jersey in practice. He left the Bills’ Week 2 game last Thursday and did not return with this shoulder injury. It’s a good sign that he is practicing but the non-contact jersey indicates Moore still has a ways to go before being cleared to play Week 3 against the Chargers.

item.title: Giants WR Malik Nabers (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers hurt his shoulder in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams, staying in the game and catching zero passes after the injury. The Giants had a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, listing Nabers as limited. When asked if the 23-year-old had X-rays done, head coach John Harbaugh gave his usual vague answer, saying, “I don’t know.” A limited practice listing indicates Nabers is not dealing with a major issue, but his practice status is worth monitoring leading up to Week 3 against the Titans.

Source: Pat Leonard

item.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (rib) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey was a full participant in practice after getting in a limited practice last week and playing in Week 2 against the Raiders. The 24-year-old was limited by both the injury and the Chargers’ stagnant offense but looks to be healing enough to practice fully this week. McConkey is trending to play Week 3 against the Bills, where he will be in the low-end WR2 mix.

item.title: Chargers OT Rashawn Slater (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rashawn Slater LAC Tackle

Slater popped up on the injury report with a groin issue, getting in a limited practice Wednesday. Multiple other members of the Chargers’ offensive line were also in the injury report, with G Cole Strange (pec) getting in a limited practice and G/T Trey Pipkins (knee) and G Kayode Awosika (fibula) not practicing. There is no indication yet that Slater will miss time but the Chargers offensive line is already banged up early in the season.

item.title: Jordan Whittington (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jordan Whittington

Whittington missed Week 2 with the quad injury and doesn’t look likely to return this week. Xavier Smith and Konata Mumpfield each ran a little over half of the routes last week, though they combined for just three targets. With Tutu Atwell also in the mix for the WR2 role, there isn’t a clear fantasy winner here despite the bevy of injuries.

item.title: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Coming off a nine-target day, the Rams are likely giving their new No. 2 receiver a maintenance day, though this is still an injury report to keep an eye on throughout the week. Puka Nacua, Jordan Whittington, and Colby Parkinson were all on the sidelines for today’s practice. With even just Nacua out, Ferguson projects for a TE1 fantasy role. The other injuries will help push him up the Week 3 ranks.

item.title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims is still working his way back after aggravating his foot injury in Week 1 against the Chiefs. Although his early participation is a good sign for his Week 3 availability, the Broncos will likely play things extra cautiously this time around.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Colby Parkinson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

The Rams have leaned on multi-TE sets when Puka Nacua has missed time or been limited over the past year, so losing Parkinson would be another notable loss for the offense. Even if he plays, this injury all but locks in Terrance Ferguson as the team’s de facto WR2 for Week 3, assuming Nacua remains sidelined. Ferguson is pushing for a TE1 ranking ahead of his Week 3 date with the Broncos.

item.title: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

What a strange turn of events. Earlier this week, Coleman was viewed as the Broncos’ potential Week 3 starter. Now, RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) and RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) are both practicing in a limited capacity while Coleman works in the training room. The rookie running back remains a worthwhile stash, but he may be unable to play this week.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jalen McMillan (knee) is practicing in full for Week 3 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

McMillan logged three full practices last week but was limited to just seven snaps on Sunday. He was not targeted once. His role should increase as he gets more practice reps under his belt, but fantasy managers can’t count on that happening this week specifically. He is not on the fantasy menu for Week 3.

item.title: Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey strained his hamstring in Week 1 and logged two limited sessions in Week 2 practices before being declared inactive on game day. His continued limited practice participation puts him on track to backup starting RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring), who is also rehabbing after experiencing cramps in Week 2. RB3 Jonah Coleman (ankle) is currently sidelined.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Hamstring cramps forced Dobbins out of the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars. Follow-up reports on the issue have been positive, and it sounds like he has a real chance to play in Week 3 against the Rams, potentially as the leader of a banged-up committee. Keep an eye on his practice participation this week.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Baker Mayfield (illness) is practicing in full for Week 3 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield didn’t speak to reporters after practice because of the illness, but the team didn’t limit his practice reps. It’s possible the Bucs lighten his workload over the next two days, but he should be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Vikings. Mayfield will look to get back on track after a sluggish start to the season. He has fallen into the QB2 ranks until further notice.

item.title: DeeJay Dallas (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
DeeJay Dallas MIN Running Back

Dallas should be fine by the time Sunday rolls around, but it’s worth noting given how thin the Vikings are at running back. Jordan Mason is on injured reserve and Aaron Jones came out of Week 2 with a knee injury. He did not practice today and his Week 3 availability is very much in question. Dallas and Demond Claiborne will split the Minnesota backfield if Jones is out. The toe injury could force Kevin O’Connell to give Claiborne a few more touches this week.

item.title: Rams placed Ronnie Rivers (calf) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Ronnie Rivers

Sean McVay said Rivers will miss 4-6 weeks. The team will call up one of Dean Connor or Jordan Waters from the practice squad for Week 3. Rivers doesn’t play much on offense, but he would normally be in line for backup duties if something happened to Kyren Williams or Blake Corum.

item.title: Trent Brown (knee/wrist) did not practice Wednesdaay.
item.description:
Trent Brown HOU Tackle

Ed Ingram remained sidelined with a groin injury. He did not play in Week 2. Brown had been playing through the wrist issue, but the knee injury is new. With Nico Collins banged up, the last thing Houston needs is another offensive line injury. Blake Fisher would take Brown’s spot at right tackle if he can’t suit up on Sunday.

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

That makes two consecutive limited sessions for Bowers, who resumed practicing on Friday last week. The Raiders’ star tight end and No. 1 pass catcher is on track to play this week against the Saints and can be treated as an elite TE1, as usual, assuming this is the case. It would be great to see Bowers resume practicing in full tomorrow. Stay tuned.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) will not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Sean McVay was unsure if Nacua would be able to play in Week 3 when asked about it on Tuesday. A DNP today suggests Nacua will need at least one more week of rest before returning to the lineup. Terrance Ferguson finished second on the Rams in targets last week with nine. He caught six passes for 54 yards and a score. No receiver outside of Davante Adams was targeted more than two times. Adams was utterly dominant, turning his 10 targets into 195 yards and two scores. Those are the only two major beneficiaries of Nacua’s likely absence.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Cardinals placed CB Will Johnson (neck) on injured reserve
item.description:
Will Johnson ARI Cornerback

Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said on Monday that Johnson (neck) could miss the remainder of the season. ESPN’s Adam Schefter broke the news today about Johnson being placed on injured reserve, though he did not specify whether Johnson’s season is for sure over. Cardinals slot CB Garrett Williams (Achilles) and perimeter CB2 Max Melton (toe) are also dealing with injuries.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Giants coach John Harbaugh kept “open the possibility for a postseason return” for QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
item.description:
Jaxson Dart NYG Quarterback

Garafolo notes that a meniscus repair typically requires a 4-6 month recovery timeline. If Dart heals at the fastest possible speed, he could return in late January. This seems somewhat unlikely, given the fact that he will also have his MCL surgically fixed and must rehab the injured PCL, but apparently Harbaugh is feeling optimistic. In the meantime, QB Jameis Winston has been named the starter.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports that Jameis Winston is the Giants’ starting quarterback, but a trade for another quarterback “is possible.”
item.description:
Jameis Winston NYG Quarterback

Winston played poorly in QB Jaxson Dart’s (knee) stead last week. If he can bounce back, the trade talk might calm down. If not, it will only get louder. The Giants face the Titans in Week 3, which should provide Winston with an opportunity to reasonably support one or two pass catchers in fantasy. Stay tuned.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

Hendrickson recently broke his finger “into several pieces.” Ouch. Hendrickson played through the pain last week, collecting six quarterback pressures and one sack. We expect him to suit up again in Week 3, though the team will manage his reps.

Source: Calvin Watkins

item.title: Jaylen Wright (stinger/foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright and Ollie Gordon each have three carries this year. De’Von Achane has 31. Even if the backup role gets narrowed to just Gordon, there isn’t any fantasy value to be had behind Achane.

item.title: Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and now opens this week not practicing. The 27-year-old suffered the injury in Week 1 and has yet to return to practice since then. The Commanders’ tight end depth chart is thin and neither John Bates or Ben Sinnott are worth rostering with Jayden Daniels out.

item.title: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Javon Kinlaw WAS Defensive Tackle

Kinlaw dealt with a back injury last week but played in Week 2. He came out of the loss against the Cowboys with an additional injury to the shoulder. Kinlaw’s status for Week 3 is in question as he sits out of practice with back and shoulder issues.

item.title: Chris Bell (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

This could just be maintenance for a player who is likely still on a pitch count as he continues to put distance between himself and his 2025 torn ACL. On the other hand, Bell has not been on the injury report before today, so we’re at least a little bit concerned. With Caleb Douglas banged up, Bell would have been in line for more routes this week. That’s far less likely now.

item.title: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Chris Jones KC Defensive Tackle

Jones played through the injury last week. His continued practice participation this week is a good sign. He should be good to go for a favorable D/ST matchup against the Dolphins this week.

Source: Pete Sweeney

item.title: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Barion Brown NO Wide Receiver

Brown generally contributes as a gadget receiver and in the return game. Were he to sit out in Week 3, his absence would likely be a bigger deal for the Saints than it would be for fantasy managers.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter was technically ruled out because of his back injury last week. The Steelers aren’t even bothering to list it this time around. The two sides remain at an impasse over a contract extension, and their relationship seems to be spiraling toward a point of no return. We would not expect Porter to return to action for Week 3 versus the Bengals.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman didn’t practice once last week, so a limited session today is a big step in the right direction. Germie Bernard took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and caught four passes for 35 yards, but he also coughed up a drop that was then intercepted by New England. The mistake all but guarantees his return to the bench once Pittman is healthy.

item.title: Titans RB Tyjae Spears (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears and starting RB Tony Pollard were both sidelined by ankle injuries today. If the two players are unable to go, rookie RB Nicholas Singleton is the next player up. He is worth stashing on fantasy football benches at this time.

Source: Tennessee Titans

item.title: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren got a little banged up in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots, but he’s still the team’s healthiest running back of note. Rico Dowdle was in a boot today after injuring his toe in Week 2. He was listed as a DNP and appears to be on the wrong side of questionable to start the week. Even at less than full strength, Warren would likely handle the bulk of the backfield snaps if Dowdle can’t go.

item.title: Jonathan Allen (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jonathan Allen CIN Defensive Tackle

Fellow defensive tackle B.J. Hill (Achilles) was also held out of practice. He missed Week 2 and looks likely to sit for at least one more game. Cincy signed Allen to a two-year deal in the offseason. He has already made a big impact with one sack in each of his first two games.

item.title: Titans RB Tony Pollard (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

We were told earlier today that Pollard and Spears are “dealing with some soreness.” Now we know what ails them. The Titans field an unexciting offense, but on the off chance that both Pollard and Spears are unable to play, rookie RB Nicholas Singleton would theoretically be in line for a sizable workload against the Giants this week. Stay tuned.

Source: Tennessee Titans

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Giants EDGE Brian Burns (ankle) “is not expected to need surgery but is likely to miss some time.”
item.description:
Brian Burns NYG Outside Linebacker

Burns, 28, has had poor injury luck in recent seasons. He currently accounts for three quarterback pressures and three tackles. The Giants field a deep pass-rushing unit, though, so their D/ST should be okay against the Titans in Week 3.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet will not return to practice this week.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Charbonnet still has to sit out two more games while on the PUP list, but he’s eligible to have his three-week practice window opened. That won’t happen this week, though it doesn’t give us much info on his return timeline. Macdonald previously said Charbonnet remained on track with his aggressive timetable, which is, again, rather vague. Fantasy managers with an IR spot can consider stashing Charbonnet, but he’s not worth the roster spot otherwise.

Source: Corbin Smith

item.title: Jets EDGE David Bailey (elbow) is practicing in full for Week 3 against the Lions.
item.description:
David Bailey NYJ Defensive End

Bailey should be good to go for Week 3. Fellow Jets EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) is limited to begin the week, and S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) remains sidelined. The Lions’ offensive line is banged up. Having both pass rushers available would be helpful.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) was removed from the injury report for Week 3 against the Packers.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

Tagovailoa joins a jumbled Falcons backup quarterback group for Thursday Night Football. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. The Falcons will start QB Michael Penix (knee).

Source: Marc Raimondi

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Kaye reports Austin Ekeler is not expected to sign with the Panthers today.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler

Ekeler worked out for the Panthers today. Kaye noted that the workout went well, so it’s possible Ekeler lands with the team in the future. With Jonathon Brooks (groin) on injured reserve, the Panthers need to make an addition or two at running back, even just for some extra depth. Regardless of who they sign, Chuba Hubbard is set for a workhorse role for the foreseeable future.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: 49ers placed DT CJ West on injured reserve with a knee injury.
item.description:
CJ West SF Defensive Tackle

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said West suffered a bone chip in his knee. The injury will require surgery. He is expected to return this season. The 49ers correspondingly signed DT Naquan Jones to the active roster and DT Viliami Fehoko to the practice squad, and released CB Jakob Robinson.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Devin Lloyd (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Devin Lloyd CAR Linebacker

Lloyd was one of the Panthers’ premier free agent additions this offseason, and he’s already proven to be worth the investment. Lloyd terrorized the Falcons in Week 2 with a sack and two interceptions, one of which was a pick-six. Fellow free agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips was also absent from practice today. He is dealing with a back injury. Though the Browns aren’t a particularly good offense right now, it would still be a massive boon for them if Lloyd and Phillips are out for Week 3.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Monday that Evans would have to be managed this week. Sitting out on Wednesday is hardly surprising and not overly concerning. The 33-year-old wide receiver missed plenty of practice this summer and has looked great thus far. As long as he’s back at it by Friday, we are not concerned.

Source: Vic Tafur

item.title: Seahawks placed OG Anthony Bradford on injured reserve with a knee injury.
item.description:
Anthony Bradford SEA Guard

Bradford missed Week 2 and will now miss at least four more games with the knee injury. The Seahawks also signed S Rodney Thomas to the active roster and signed DT

Source: Bob Condotta

item.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker played through the ankle issue last week and tallied eight catches for 66 yards. He didn’t appear hampered by the injury in the slightest. The team will likely manage his reps in practice for the next few weeks, but there’s no reason to believe he’s at risk of missing Week 3’s game against Cleveland. After two strong performances to start the year, Coker is firmly entrenched in the WR3 ranks. He could crack the top-24 with another big game.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (shoulder) will practice this week, but his Wednesday participation level has not yet been determined.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

If Price does practice today, we expect it to be a limited session, since Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald doesn’t even know if Price will suit up today. Fantasy managers should tentatively expect Price to play in Week 3 against the Commanders, but the situation still seems fluid. Seahawks RB Emanuel Wilson will likely remain involved if Price is active. He would take on lead rushing duties if Price cannot go.

Source: Curtis Crabtree

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold (glute) will resume practicing, but won’t take every rep on Wednesday.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

This means Darnold will likely be listed as a limited participant today. The plan is to ramp him up as the week goes on, and Macdonald said the team would like to have a decision by Friday on whether Darnold will face the Commanders this week. The Seahawks’ quarterback has been sidelined since straining a glute tendon in Week 1. He will probably need to be treated as a QB2 with QB1 upside in his first game back, but his practice participation will clarify his readiness.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Brenen Thompson did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

Thompson injured his hip during the preseason and was on the Week 1 injury report as a limited participant twice. He was eventually cleared and has played in both of LA’s losses. Thompson wasn’t on the injury report last week, so this could be a new issue. Either way, the rookie appears to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar, but his absence could get Tre’ Harris on the field for a few more routes.

Source: Alex Insdorf

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss said he expects Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) to be listed as a non-participant on Wednesday.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

This is a bit confusing because Raridon suited up for practice. He did not participate on the main field, though, so Reiss thinks he will be listed as a DNP. A limited listing is possible, but we default to the ESPN reporter here. Raridon does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues, but remains a viable stash in deep leagues.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) is not expected to travel to Brazil for Week 3 against the Ravens.
item.description:
DeMarvion Overshown DAL Linebacker

Overshown will now, apparently, miss his second game this season. He will be missed. The Cowboys’ defense is tasked with stymying the Ravens’ top-tier rushing attack, led by RB Derrick Henry and QB Lamar Jackson.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

Etienne begins the week with a limited session, which is either good or bad, depending on when the injury occurred. If this is a lingering issue from Sunday, Etienne should be considered likely to play. Limited practices early in the week are generally a good sign. However, if he suffered the injury during today’s practice, his Week 3 availability would be in jeopardy. Veteran Saints RB Alvin Kamara would likely get the start, but RB Kendre Miller would be FLEX-viable if Etienne sits.

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jonah Coleman suffered a sprained ankle in Week 2 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

RJ Harvey missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury and J.K. Dobbins left the game early with what was eventually called leg cramps. It’s unclear if any of the three Denver backs will be available for Week 3. Dobbins appears most likely to suit up, though nothing is guaranteed. Tyler Badie could ultimately be the team’s starting running back on Sunday. He should be stashed in most fantasy leagues in case all three starting options ahead of him are ruled out.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

Source: Kris Rhim

item.title: Aaron Jones (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones tweaked his knee in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears. He ultimately played through the issue during the second half and racked up 23 carries for 105 yards. Head coach Kevin O’Connell said he was “pretty sore” after the game. ESPN’s Kevin Seifert added today that Jones playing in Week 3 is “not a sure thing.” Jones simply can’t handle that large of a workload at this point in his career, and the team will likely get DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne more involved this week, even if Jones is able to suit up. If he can’t, those two backs will likely split the backfield.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: Bills DT T.J. Sanders underwent an appendectomy on Tuesday.
item.description:
T.J. Sanders BUF Defensive Tackle

A knee injury sidelined Sanders in Week 1 and continued to limit him in Week 2 practices. Midweek, he had an illness designation added to his injury report listing. Now we know why. It could be a couple more weeks until we see the Bills’ 2025 second-round pick take the field this season.

Source: Lance Lysowski
